name: Imran Khan Cancer Appeal USA
mission: TO GENERATE CHARITABLE DONATIONS FOR HELPING IN THE TREATMENT OF CANCER IN THIRD WORLD COUNTRIES AND THE ESTABLISHMENT OF THE SHAUKAT KHANUM MEMORIAL CANCER HOSPITAL AND RESEARCH CENTER. SPECIFIC GOALS INCLUDE (1) TO INITIATE CHARITABLE FUND RAISING ACTIVITIES, (2) TO RECRUIT PROFESSIONAL AND NON- PROFESSIONAL STAFF AND EXPENSES FOR THE ADMINISTRATIVE OFFICE, (3) TO SUPPLY FINANCIAL SUPPORT FOR THE PAYMENT OF MEDICINES, DIAGNOSTIC AND THERAPEUTIC EQUIPMENT FOR THE SHAUKAT KHANUM MEMORIAL CANCER HOSPITAL AND RESEARCH CENTER. (4) TO ASSIST IN THE RECRUITMENT OF ALL MEDICAL AND ANCILLARY PERSONNEL FOR THE SHAUKAT KHANUM MEMORIAL CANCER HOSPITAL AND RESEARCH CENTER.

rich_narrative.summary: Founded in <cite id="1">1994</cite>, Imran Khan Cancer Appeal, Inc. (IKCA) serves as a vital financial lifeline for specialized oncology care in Pakistan. The organization primarily supports the Shaukat Khanum Memorial Cancer Hospital and Research Centre, providing <cite id="2">diagnostic and clinical services</cite> to patients who otherwise could not afford treatment. In FY2024, the charity demonstrated significant growth, reporting <cite id="3">total revenue of $17,974,012</cite> to fund its medical mission. IKCA maintains a <cite id="4">95/100 overall score from Charity Navigator</cite>, reflecting a high standard of financial accountability. The charity operates with extreme fiscal leanest, reporting a <cite id="5">97.4% program expense ratio</cite> in its most recent filings. This ensures that nearly every dollar donated is directed toward <cite id="6">pharmacy, education, and clinical training</cite> programs. While the organization excels in financial efficiency, it maintains a balanced profile due to governance structures that rely on a <cite id="7">single-member board of directors</cite>, which presents a departure from standard non-profit oversight models. For Muslim donors, the charity offers <cite id="8">verified zakat-eligible programs</cite> that specifically serve the poor and needy (fuqara and masakin) facing life-threatening illnesses.
